Reserved-word column names: SalesTerritory."Group", ProductProductPhoto."Primary" — need quoting.
Empty table Customer (0 rows): original_values empty, original_sizes 0; FK children (SalesOrderHeader.CustomerID) draw from empty parent -> NULLs.

FKs declared inline without parent column (Address.StateProvinceID references StateProvince; BillOfMaterials.*; CurrencyRate.*; Product.*; Document.Owner; StateProvince.*; EmployeeDepartmentHistory.*; EmployeePayHistory.*; JobCandidate.*; SalesOrderHeader.*) — pragma returns NULL parent col, must default to same name.
SalesOrderHeader.ShipMethodID references Address(AddressID) — semantically wrong parent (should be ShipMethod); FK is real in DDL, keep it.
SalesOrderDetail has composite FK (SpecialOfferID,ProductID) -> SpecialOfferProduct(SpecialOfferID,ProductID); pragma foreign_key_list yields two separate rows, not one composite edge.
Self-ish chain: Person.BusinessEntityID -> BusinessEntity; Employee -> Person; SalesPerson -> Employee; Store -> SalesPerson; Customer -> Store/Person/SalesTerritory; deep FK levels.

All DATETIME/DATE columns stored as TEXT with format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.0' (or 'YYYY-MM-DD' for DATE columns BirthDate/HireDate/StartDate/EndDate in Employee/EmployeeDepartmentHistory/ProductCostHistory/ProductListPriceHistory).
CountryRegion.ModifiedDate has a literal string 'ModifiedDate' as a value (data corruption) — Date template detection may pick a non-date element.
BLOB columns (ProductPhoto.ThumbNailPhoto/LargePhoto, Document.Document) stored as TEXT hex '0x...' — storage class contradicts declared BLOB; TS dispatches BLOB to String.
Shift.StartTime/EndTime declared TEXT (not TIME) so TS uses String fuzzer, not Time fuzzer — times like '07:00:00' will be replaced by random strings.

Many INTEGER PKs are autoincrement with notnull=0 (ProductCategory, ProductDescription, ProductModel, ProductPhoto, SalesReason, SalesTerritory, ScrapReason, Shift, ShipMethod, SpecialOffer, Address, AddressType, BusinessEntity, ContactType, CurrencyRate, Department, Location, PhoneNumberType, Product, CreditCard, SalesOrderHeader, PurchaseOrderHeader, PurchaseOrderDetail, WorkOrder, TransactionHistory, ProductReview, ShoppingCartItem, SalesTaxRate, ProductSubcategory, ProductCostHistory, ProductListPriceHistory, ProductInventory, ProductProductPhoto, ProductDocument, ProductVendor, ProductModelProductDescriptionCulture, BusinessEntityAddress, BusinessEntityContact, EmailAddress, PersonCreditCard, SalesPersonQuotaHistory, SalesTerritoryHistory, SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason, SalesOrderDetail, SpecialOfferProduct, WorkOrderRouting, EmployeeDepartmentHistory, EmployeePayHistory, JobCandidate, BillOfMaterials, Document, StateProvince, ProductReview) — TS Number fuzzer will produce non-autoincrement values, insert may fail on PK conflict.

Large tables: SalesOrderDetail 121317, TransactionHistory 113443, TransactionHistoryArchive 89253, WorkOrder 72591, WorkOrderRouting 67131, SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason 27647, BusinessEntity 20777, Person 19972, EmailAddress 19972, Password 19972, Address 19614, BusinessEntityAddress 19614, PersonCreditCard 19118, CreditCard 19118, CurrencyRate 13532 — read_schema sampling needed.

Unique constraints on multi-column tuples (Shift(StartTime,EndTime), Address(AddressLine1,AddressLine2,City,StateProvinceID,PostalCode), BillOfMaterials(ProductAssemblyID,ComponentID,StartDate), CurrencyRate(CurrencyRateDate,FromCurrencyCode,ToCurrencyCode), Document(DocumentLevel,DocumentNode), StateProvince(StateProvinceCode,CountryRegionCode), SalesTaxRate(StateProvinceID,TaxType)) — TS drop_unique_duplicates only handles single-column unique, so these may fail at insert.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer with template '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.0' for DATETIME columns (first parsable element sets template); DATE columns (BirthDate, HireDate, StartDate, EndDate) template '%Y-%m-%d'.

Date fuzzer range from min/max of parsed elements — e.g. Employee.BirthDate range ~1952-1990, HireDate ~2007-2009; fresh dates stay in that narrow window, so queries filtering on year ranges may still match.
String fuzzer for all TEXT columns: random strings over 'a-zA-Z 0-9()' length 0-20, plus contamination; names like 'Ken','Terri' become gibberish — LIKE/equality on names will miss.
String fuzzer for rowguid: 20-char random strings, not GUID format — queries filtering rowguid format will miss.
String fuzzer for EmailAddress: random strings, not emails — email LIKE '%@%' queries will miss.

Number fuzzer for INTEGER PKs: uniform in [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1] then perturbed +-1/+-2 — tiny values, not the original 1..N range; joins on PK still work but range filters (e.g. BusinessEntityID > 1000) will miss.
Number fuzzer for REAL columns: uniform in [-10^4,10^4] (scale=4 default) — SalesYTD ~7.8M original becomes ~thousands; range filters on large amounts will miss.
Number fuzzer for INTEGER non-PK (Quantity, OrderQty, Rating, ExpYear): uniform [-1,1] perturbed — ExpYear 2006 becomes ~0; year filters miss.
FK consistency: child FK values drawn from parent's final column values with replacement — joins work, but parent PKs are tiny random ints so FK distribution is skewed.

Empty Customer table: SalesOrderHeader.CustomerID gets NULLs (parent empty) — but CustomerID is NOT NULL, so all SalesOrderHeader rows fail insert; SalesOrderHeader ends up empty, cascading to SalesOrderDetail/SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason.

Composite PK tables (SalesOrderDetail, WorkOrderRouting, etc.) get PK-duplicate rows dropped, but single-column unique columns (rowguid, Name, AccountNumber) get drop_unique_duplicates — many rows lost.
CHECK constraints: none declared in this DDL, so checked=False everywhere; p=0.2 default fuzz probability applies.
